what_was_said: That CEMLA lived at cemla.org
what_is_true: cemla.org is a Mexican central-banking body. The arrivals index is at cemla.com/buscador/
how_it_was_caught: David went to the address given and found the wrong institution.

what_was_said: That Mary Ann Hellen Brayley was a new find
what_is_true: She had been in data/taylor-line.tsv since 8 September, from David's own MyHeritage tree. What findmypast supplied was a citation - the baptism of 30 Oct 1884 at Northam, ref 1843A/PR/1/16 - not the fact.
how_it_was_caught: David: "why is her mothers name new? its been in my myheritage tree forever."

what_was_said: That the Rosario marriage index showed "Larena V x Sarmiento A" at Libro 9 folio 20 - and that this was a candidate
what_is_true: The entry reads *** LAVENA V. x BELMONTE A. ***. It was misread at low resolution and kept a false candidate alive for two days.
how_it_was_caught: Read again at the film's maximum resolution on 10 September. Not close: the hand is unambiguous.

what_was_said: That a cluster of Larena/Lerena at Cayasta might be a kindred
what_is_true: Cayasta is an ITALIAN colony - Laurini five times, Lauron, Castelarin - and the same mother is transcribed Azela in one act and Raiela in another. The "cluster" was a transcription artefact.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the acts instead of the index. Retracted publicly; the register entry is now EXCLUDED.

what_was_said: That the 1869 census showed a Llerena HOUSEHOLD at Rosario
what_is_true: The image shows twelve separately-numbered, unrelated individuals in a conventillo. There is ONE man of the name, Bartolome, not a family.
how_it_was_caught: Opening the image instead of trusting the index grouping.

what_was_said: That Gabino L. Llerena was a Rosario-born link between the two countries
what_is_true: Every other person on his record is Uruguayan, so the Rosario in question is Rosario, COLONIA, in Uruguay.
how_it_was_caught: Caught before it was published, by reading the rest of the record.

what_was_said: That reading the Rosario registers needed the Chrome extension, because the in-app browser could not crop
what_is_true: Wrong twice. The viewer has its own zoom, and - far more important - the Image Index panel is an HTML TABLE. The handwriting never needed to be read at all.
how_it_was_caught: David: "why do you need chrome? use your own browser?"

what_was_said: That "Armand[o] Lorena", born 1882 at Rosario de Lerma, Salta, was "probably not him" - written off on four objections
what_is_true: It IS him. The image reads "Clase de 1882 / LERENA - Pablo Armando / hijo de JUAN CARLOS LERENA y de MARIA LERENA / Nacido en Rosario de Santa Fe / Oficina enroladora de CAPETOWN". Three of the four objections were artefacts of a machine index that dropped "Pablo", moved him 1,400 km, wrote Lerena as Lorena, and invented the surname "Serena" out of the printed word SERIE.
how_it_was_caught: Opening the image. It took two minutes. *** This is the most serious error in the archive: the central finding of the project was nearly discarded. ***

what_was_said: That Roque's first wife was "Rosalina Wilhelmina CHAPPELL", read from a marriage index
what_is_true: CHAPPELL was her MARRIED name. She was Roseline Wilhelmina FORBES, widow of Frederick Christian Chappell. The 1936 register calls her "Rosaline Wilhermina Forbes Chappell" because that is what a remarrying widow is called.
how_it_was_caught: The 1920 Chappell-Forbes marriage, found in BOTH the civil and the Anglican registers, plus Chappell's own estate file.

what_was_said: Margin readings taken from register openings rendered at 42% scale
what_is_true: Not reliable. At that size "Timoteo Lucero" was read as "Armando Sara" - both words wrong, and an L-surname missed, which is the exact failure that matters when hunting one L-surname. Every opening was re-read from the margin strips at maximum resolution.
how_it_was_caught: Zooming on a single doubtful entry, and finding it was not doubtful at all - it was simply wrong.

what_was_said: That the Lerena palette was identical to the FALCO archive's, with hex values quoted
what_is_true: The values quoted were Falco's, not ours. The Lerena styles.css is byte-identical to the DEFRANCESKI archive's. Falco is the outlier, with a warm palette against the shared cool one.
how_it_was_caught: Reading both files side by side instead of trusting memory.

what_was_said: That there were 29 places in the register
what_is_true: 28. "arr. Buenos Aires 1907-07-14" had been sitting as its own one-person place beside the 43-person "Buenos Aires - arrivals" because the normalising pattern only matched "arr. YYYY".
how_it_was_caught: Looking at a person page that had no business having its own place.

what_was_said: Layout: a bare "6" floating in the middle of a sentence on every person page
what_is_true:
.prose is a flex COLUMN, not a paragraph class. Using it on a

made every inline its own row.
how_it_was_caught: Looking at the rendered page rather than the built HTML.

what_was_said: That the Italian-origin hypothesis was "the most consequential thing on this page"
what_is_true: Within the hour, the low-confidence genetic groups showed no Italian group among the five legible ones - evidence against it. Downgraded the same day to "already weaker than when it was written".
how_it_was_caught: The next screenshot.

what_was_said: That the four LERINA arrivals of 1889 were excluded because "LERINA here is an Italian surname, not a variant of the Spanish Lerena"
what_is_true: They ARE excluded, but on their dates and the composition of the party: they arrive in 1889 aged 59, 55, 21 and 17, seven years after Pablo Armando was born at Rosario, and the party contains no Juan Carlos and no Maria. The claim about the SURNAME is withdrawn as a reason - it was reached from an index without opening the manifest, which is the move that got the Armando Lorena card wrong.
how_it_was_caught: This archive's own search box, which showed all four LERINA entries carrying the same unexamined label.

what_was_said: That the Arturo Lerena in army drawer Cajon 985 was born at Montevideo in 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel
what_is_true: Two men. The Uruguayan record relied on gives the wife as EMA REGULES, and Ema Regules married JUAN ARTURO Lerena Traibel (1861-1936), whose children were born at Montevideo 1881-87. The Arturo in the drawer married AMALIA DIAZ and had children in La Pampa, Mendoza and Entre Rios 1889-97. The row is withdrawn and a "four branches" claim became three.
how_it_was_caught: Opening the FamilySearch Tree profile the record was attached to - going to the underlying record, which is the move this archive keeps having to relearn.

what_was_said: Every person page showed an empty children list unless somebody had separately written an explicit "child" row
what_is_true: A link is written once in data/relations.tsv - "X, father, Y" - and the builder recorded it on X's page and never reversed it onto Y's. Thirty-eight parent edges were read one way against fifteen compensating child rows. Pablo Armando, Juan Carlos, Maria Lerena, Mary Septima Taylor, Roque, Roseline Forbes and Doreen Chappell all had children in the data and none on their charts. Fixed in the builder, with aliases excluded so a machine-index variant is not counted as a second child.
how_it_was_caught: Wiring in the Montevideo household, whose four documented children rendered as none.

what_was_said: Nothing, visibly - which is why it went unnoticed
what_is_true: The people builder looked people up by name, and ELEVEN NAMES appeared twice or three times in the register - three Francisco Lerenas, three Jose Llerenas, two Carlos Lerenas, two Gilbertos. The later row silently won and thirteen rows could not be addressed at all. No edge happened to name an ambiguous person, so nothing looked wrong - but the next edge added would have attached to the wrong man in silence. Duplicates now carry a distinguishing tag and the builder REFUSES TO BUILD if two rows share a name.
how_it_was_caught: Caught on the way to adding twenty-four relationship edges, several of them to a "Carlos LERENA" and a "Gilberto LERENA".

what_was_said: "Of the 1 relationships in the chart above"
what_is_true: A plural where the count can be one. Three people pages carried it.
how_it_was_caught: An audit of all 138 person pages after the chart builder was changed.

what_was_said: 129 people in the register
what_is_true: 138, and climbing. The figure was typed by hand, correct when written and stale within days. It now derives from the data, like everything else on this site - the whole method being that pages are generated from the TSVs so page and data cannot drift. This one had escaped it.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the front page instead of assuming it.

what_was_said: Paragraphs on six pages silently broke every emphasised phrase onto its own line
what_is_true:
The .prose rule is a CONTAINER style - display:flex, flex-direction:column, gap:16px - meant for a
wrapping several paragraphs. It had also been put on 21 individual

elements, and a flex container blockifies its children: every and directly inside those paragraphs became a full-width block on its own line. About 27 phrases across /searched/, /argentina/, /taylor/, /register/, /method/ and /people/ read as broken-up fragments rather than sentences. Fixed with one rule, p.prose{display:block}, which keeps the intended 80ch measure.
how_it_was_caught: Looking at the page in a browser after adding a section, and not believing the explanation that it was my own markup - the CSS had no rule matching the element, so the cause had to be inherited from the parent.

what_was_said: The archive emphasised things to its readers as *** like this ***
what_is_true: The TSVs mark emphasis with triple asterisks and NOTHING EVER CONVERTED IT. 362 of them were rendering to readers across 38 pages - 132 on the register alone - so the archive was showing its own working notation as if it were text. Now converted at render time by site/src/lib/text.js, and check-links.py fails the build if a marker ever reaches a page again.
how_it_was_caught: Counting them, after noticing a pair of asterisks on the gaps page while fixing something else.

what_was_said: The sources page said "Everything consulted so far" while listing nothing after 10 September
what_is_true: It listed 12 sources and had not moved for three days, while the Montevideo household, the Rosario death index, 750 acts of the 1882 register, the full-text density measurement and Sancho's six spellings all went unrecorded. *** On a page whose entire purpose is letting a reader check the work, that heading was a false claim. *** It is now generated from data/sources-consulted.tsv - 33 sources, 13 of them PRIMARY - so it cannot fall behind again.
how_it_was_caught: Auditing my own list of what to do next, and finding the page contradicted the archive.

what_was_said: That Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas and Julia Juanico had FIVE children
what_is_true: *** SEVEN. *** Jose Julio, born 15 March 1879, and Candido Jaime, born 13 September 1884, were both missing. The five came from working outward from Julia's 1910 death certificate, which names five - and a death certificate is a list of the children who mattered to whoever registered the death, not a list of the children a woman bore. Found by searching the PARENTS' names directly instead.
how_it_was_caught: Doing the obvious search that had not been done: both parents' names, in one query, across every Uruguayan collection.

what_was_said: That the Trinidad, Flores kindred included a daughter of Luis and Julia
what_is_true: It did not, and that row linked the Montevideo trunk to the Trinidad kindred when nothing links them. "Luis x Julia, Emma Liseta 1876" was read off a findmypast list that gives mothers BY FIRST NAME ONLY, so the Montevideo couple looked like a Trinidad couple. She is *** Emma Sixta Lerena Juanico, born and baptised at Montevideo *** - our own trunk. The note's own prose said eleven Trinidad children while its table showed twelve; nobody had reconciled the two.
how_it_was_caught: Testing the register's search box with the term its own placeholder suggested - "Trinidad" - and getting nothing back.

what_was_said: Ema Sixta Lerena Juanico born c.1880
what_is_true: *** 21 November 1876. *** Three independent records agree: her civil birth registration of 30 May 1903, the Uruguay Baptisms index, and her christening at the Montevideo Catedral on 8 January 1881. The c.1880 was derived from her stated age at her 1913 marriage, and an age at marriage is the weakest date in genealogy.
how_it_was_caught: Searching both parents' names, which returned all three records side by side.

what_was_said: The register promised "every named individual this archive has found"
what_is_true: It omitted the entire *** Trinidad, Flores kindred - 29 people *** - although this archive had a whole note about them, calling them the founding kindred of the surname. The register's own search placeholder invited readers to try "Trinidad", which returned nothing at all. The people are now in it, and the placeholder is honest because the data caught up with the promise rather than the promise being weakened.
how_it_was_caught: Clicking the page's own suggested search term and watching it return zero.

what_was_said: That Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas is not in the indexed Uruguayan death registers
what_is_true: *** He is, and he died on 24 December 1901. *** Two sweeps were run and reported here as negatives - 1,502 Montevideo Lerena deaths for 1880-1911, and 132 Luis Lerena deaths for 1899-1903 - and this archive went so far as to write up the FamilySearch Tree's date of 1901 as a lead the registers appeared to contradict. The registers did not contradict it. THE INDEX DID: FamilySearch files him as "Luis SERENA Lenguas", so every search on the surname missed him. Found within the hour by searching his MOTHER, Justiniana Lenguas, instead.
how_it_was_caught: Searching on the rarest stable name in the household rather than on a surname that the clerks and the indexers between them spell Lerena, Lorena, Serena and Languas.

what_was_said: Julia Juanico born about 1844
what_is_true: *** 23 November 1842. *** The 1844 was derived from her stated age of 66 on her 1910 death registration; she was 67. Her baptism of 4 October 1843 at San Francisco de Asis gives the date, and gives her mother in full as Juliana JOAQUINA Gonzalez.
how_it_was_caught: Searching her FATHER rather than her surname - the same move that found her husband's death the same evening.

what_was_said: That Bartolome Llerena was "the only person of this surname found in Rosario before 1882"
what_is_true: Looser than the evidence allows. *** Six LORENAS are in the same 1869 census *** - Agustin, Guillermo, Geronima, Mercedes, Feliz and Maria - and this archive's own register groups LORENA with LERENA and LLERENA as spellings of one name, because the clerks disagreed. Two of them are flagged in that very register as the right age to be a parent of a child born in 1882. The note now claims only what was checked: the only person spelled Llerena or Lerena.
how_it_was_caught: A sweep of all 183 register rows against the notes that describe them - the note and the register contradicted each other.

what_was_said: That FamilySearch film image arks cannot be reached by script, so each opening must be got by driving the viewer
what_is_true: *** Wrong, and wrong because I tested the wrong URL form. *** /ark:/61903/3:1:<ARK>?i=<N> ignores the i parameter and keeps the same image - which is what I tested, and what I generalised from. /search/film/<DGS>?i=<N> RESOLVES TO IMAGE N, and the ark can be read straight out of the page title. I published the pessimistic claim in the register file and in a commit message within the hour.
how_it_was_caught: Trying the other URL form while starting the Rosario death registers, and getting a different ark back.

what_was_said: That Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas was born about 1845, and his brother was "Alberto Otario"
what_is_true: *** Born 9 FEBRUARY 1843, on the act of his own baptism *** - the 1845 came from his stated age of 56 on his death registration, and an age at death is an estimate. And his brother is *** ALBERTO OCTAVIO ***, not Alberto Otario; the latter is how FamilySearch indexed a hand that plainly reads Octavio. Their sister, indexed as "Justinia", is JUSTINIANA MAURICIA MAXIMA.
how_it_was_caught: Opening the 1846 and 1850 baptism images instead of trusting the index that summarised them.

what_was_said: A row asserting that Maria E. C. Lerena, born 1869, was a daughter of Gilberto Lerena, born 1854
what_is_true: He would have been *** FIFTEEN. *** All the record says is that she was in his household at the 1895 census; "daughter" was this archive's reading of a household, not the census's word. The row is left in place with the contradiction stated against it rather than quietly re-labelled.
how_it_was_caught: A new near-duplicate check in tools/consistency.py, which flagged her beside another Maria E. Lerena and made somebody read both rows.

what_was_said: That the Rosario confirmations of 1890 were taken sex by sex, so a boy would be in a separate run of pages
what_is_true: *** Wrong, and built out of eleven rows. *** The first eleven entries on the first page read happened to be girls, and I turned that into a structure and a search strategy. Entries 133, 135 and 138 on a later page are Domingo, Santiago and Pablo - all "hijo leg. de" - mixed straight in among the girls. There is no boys section to find and no shortcut: the whole list has to be read. The ages run from two to fourteen in one sitting, so age rules nobody in or out either.
how_it_was_caught: Reading a second page of the same register a few hours later, instead of leaving the first page as the description of it.

what_was_said: That the first wife's surname read as something like "Dille" or "Dulce"
what_is_true: *** CAROLINA OLIVA. *** The 1842 act names Luis Lerena "viudo de Dona Carolina" and I could not read the surname confidently off that page, so I wrote down what it looked like and said it was not confidently legible. The marriage petition of 3 September 1836, found an hour later, gives it plainly: "Dona CAROLINA OLIVA, tambien natural de esta Ciudad". The uncertain reading is left recorded rather than deleted, because the next person squinting at that word should know what it is not.
how_it_was_caught: Searching for the marriage instead of squinting harder at the word.

what_was_said: That the Sancho question was closed - "three originals against two copies is not a conflict"
what_is_true: *** REOPENED WITHIN THE HOUR BY AN ORIGINAL ACT THAT SAYS FRANCISCO. *** I argued that Luis Lerena's father is Sancho on three original acts, against two 1846 entries reading Francisco which say of themselves that they are later transcripts - and concluded the conflict was only copies against originals. Then the Catedral baptism of Justa Pastora Lerena's second child, October 1833, turned up naming her parents "FRANCISCO LERINA y Maria Fernandez". That is an ORIGINAL. The tidy argument does not survive it. *** What IS constant across every record and both spellings is MARIA FERNANDEZ, the wife. *** A double forename - Sancho Francisco - would explain everything without anyone being wrong, and is now the leading reading. Sancho's own marriage act, never opened, would settle it.
how_it_was_caught: Following a new sister, Justa Pastora Lerena, to her second child - and reading the grandparents line instead of stopping at the one that agreed with me.

what_was_said: That Don Luis Lerena's first wife was CAROLINA OLIVA
what_is_true: *** CAROLINA ORIBE. *** Recorded as Oliva twice on 14 September - once to correct an earlier "not confidently legible" reading, and stated as settled. The source of the error was FamilySearch's index of the 1836 petition, which says Oliva; I read the image expecting it and saw it. A Catedral baptism of 4 July 1837, in another book and another hand, names her "Dna CAROLINA ORIBE" as godmother beside her husband. The petition, re-opened and magnified, reads ORIBE too. *** AND THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN HYPOTHESES PAGE HAD CARRIED, FROM A SECONDARY TREE, THAT HE MARRIED FIRSTLY A DAUGHTER OF AN ORIBE - it was right, and I never checked my reading against it. ***
how_it_was_caught: Finding a second act that names her, while looking for children of that marriage.

what_was_said: That the Montevideo dispensation register holds EIGHT Lerena dispensations, every Lerena in it marrying out
what_is_true: *** A NINTH WAS FOUND, and the search that produced the eight was structurally blind. *** Jose Pedro Massera petitioned on 19 June 1913 to be dispensed one conciliar proclama in order to marry "Dona EMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO, feligresa de la metropolitana" - our own Ema Sixta, eleven days before her wedding. The search formula was "LERENA FELIGRESA", which assumes the parish follows the surname immediately. *** Her COMPOUND surname sits between the two words, so the phrase could never match - and every child of both Montevideo couples carries a compound surname. *** The conclusion that no Lerena-Lerena dispensation exists is not withdrawn, but it now rests on a search known to miss exactly the people this archive cares most about, and needs re-running.
how_it_was_caught: Searching the COMPOUND surname "Lerena Juanico" in full text - the same move that had just turned up her brother Julio as a Juez de Paz.

what_was_said: That the 1895 census shows a Lerena woman married to a Lerena man - "the pattern the whole search turns on"
what_is_true: *** OVERSTATED, AND WITHDRAWN AS EVIDENCE WITHIN THE HOUR. *** The schedule does read "Lerena de L. Josefa", and the "de L." is formed exactly as on the two lines above - that part was read correctly. The INFERENCE was too confident: "de L." can equally be the enumerator shorthand for THIS HOUSEHOLD, written against every married woman in the Lerena house. Uruguayan civil registration then turned up a JOSEFA LERENA married to FERNANDO MORATORIO, whom FamilySearch's tree attaches to Josefa Lerena Traibel 1851-1947 - the same candidate. If that is her, she was "de Moratorio" and the census tells us nothing about a Lerena-Lerena marriage. *** The claim was published as "the sharpest question in the project" on the strength of an abbreviation. ***
how_it_was_caught: Searching for the marriage I had just said would settle it, instead of stopping at the reading that suited me.

what_was_said: That the Montevideo dispensation register holds eight Lerena dispensations (revised earlier today to nine)
what_is_true: *** A TENTH, found hours after the ninth, and missed for a different reason again. *** Alfredo Lerena and Hermenegilda Carolina Gavarro, Catedral Basilica de Montevideo, 3 February 1892, dispensed of consanguinity in the third degree with atingencia to the second by Archbishop Mariano Soler personally. The sweep missed it TWO WAYS AT ONCE: the groom is written *** GERENA *** - a seventh spelling for this family, in a sentence where his own father is written LORENA - and the dispensation clause comes BEFORE the names, so the formula "Lerena el impedimento" could not match. *** The count of eight is certainly low, and the file now says so. *** What survives is narrower: no LERENA-LERENA dispensation has been found, and this family did marry kin.
how_it_was_caught: Searching the rarest name in the branch - AMBROSIA TRAIBEL - instead of the surname.

what_was_said: That Avelino Lerena is not shown to be Sancho's son, so the Lerena Traibel branch does not attach
what_is_true: *** He is, and it does - settled the same day on a parish act. *** Two baptisms of 12 March 1858 at San Francisco de Asis name the paternal grandparents of Avelino's children as SANCHO LERENA and MARIA FERNANDEZ, twice on one page. So the whole Lerena Traibel line descends from Sancho - including several people already floating unattached in this register: Mercedes Micaela and Clorinda in the dispensation table, and JUAN ARTURO, the man this archive conflated with another Arturo in its first week and had to retract.
how_it_was_caught: Searching AVELINO with AMBROSIA - the couple, not the surname.

what_was_said: That Alfredo Justiniano Lerena's middle name echoed JUSTINIANA LENGUAS, connecting the two branches
what_is_true: I noticed the echo and flagged it as worth testing. *** It is nothing: he is named for his GODFATHER, JUSTINIANO LAVALLEJA, who is on the same line of the same act. *** A tidy connection between the branches that would have been entirely wrong, and the act that raised it also killed it.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the whole act instead of stopping at the name.

what_was_said: That ALEJANDRO, baptised at La Mauricia on 7 January 1846, was "A SIXTH CHILD of Luis Lerena and Justiniana Lenguas", born 29 May 1845
what_is_true: *** HE IS A SON OF AVELINO LERENA AND AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, born 29 May 1843. *** The act reads "hijo legitimo de Avelino Serena y Ambrosia Traibel. Paternos Francisco y Maria Fernandez. Maternos Juan e Isabel Centeno. *** Padrinos LUIS [L]ERENA y JUSTINIANA LENGUAS. ***" Luis and Justiniana are his GODPARENTS - which is how this archive read them as his parents. Both the branch and the year were wrong. He is the ELDEST KNOWN CHILD of Avelino and Ambrosia, and pushes their marriage back before May 1843.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the full-text transcript of the whole page rather than the entry. The image had been opened on 13 September and the act read too quickly - the parents and the godparents sit in the same sentence, and the archive took the wrong pair.

what_was_said: That the register contained no contradictions - "245 people checked, nothing contradicts itself", printed on every build for a week
what_is_true: *** THE CHECKER COULD ONLY SEE 31 OF 246 PEOPLE. *** The sibling-gap test reads a STRUCTURED parent field that only 12.6% of the register carries; for everyone else it silently found no siblings and passed. *** The contradiction it was written to catch was sitting in the data the whole time *** - Luis Eugenio b. 9 Feb 1843 and Justiniana Mauricia b. 30 July 1843, full siblings five and a half months apart. The file's own docstring names that pair as its reason for existing.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the 1846 page for another purpose, noticing the two dates, and then asking why the checker had not said so. *** A guard that reports a clean bill of health over 12.6% of the data is worse than no guard: it manufactures confidence. *** The checker now prints its coverage and falls back to compound surnames.

what_was_said: That Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas was born 9 February 1843, on the authority of his own baptism act - published since 13 September
what_is_true: *** 9 FEBRUARY 1845. *** The act is a late copy from a legajo, and it is contradicted twice: his sister Justiniana Mauricia's act, the entry immediately above his in the same hand, gives her birth as 30 July 1843 - five and a half months before him; and his civil death registration of 24 December 1901 gives his age as FIFTY-SIX, putting his birth at about 1845. The clerk wrote "ano cuarenta y tres" in the entry above and again in the entry below. A year carried down a column is the ordinary way this happens, and 1845 is the only reading under which all three records stand.
how_it_was_caught: The consistency checker, once it was fixed to see people without a structured parent field. It flagged the five-month gap on the first run after the fix. *** The archive then went looking for a third record to break the tie rather than choosing between the two. ***

what_was_said: Three unpaired emphasis markers written into the register in one session, each caught only after a build had rendered the literal characters onto a published page
what_is_true: The slip is always the same shape: closing one emphasis and opening the next with a SINGLE marker where two are needed. *** consistency.py now checks the TSVs themselves for an odd marker count, before any page exists. *** On its first run the new check found TWO MORE that check-links.py could never have caught - one in direct-line.tsv carrying the central open question about Maria Lerena, and one written an hour earlier in sources-consulted.tsv - because check-links counts only PAIRS in rendered HTML, and a single unpaired marker leaves no pair to count.
how_it_was_caught: Adding the check after making the same mistake three times. *** The interesting part is what it found that the older guard structurally could not: a guard that looks for pairs is blind to the case of exactly one. *** And the new check then failed on THIS ROW, because the row originally quoted the markers as an example - *** the convention has no way to write a literal marker, which is now a known limit of it rather than a surprise. ***

what_was_said: That Horace A Taylor married "(? Mary Jane Bridge)" - carried from a MyHeritage tree, hedged with the archive's own question mark
what_is_true: *** HE IS HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR and she is MARY JANE MARSHALL. *** Banns called at Northam, Devon, on 17 December 1893, when he was twenty-one - the earliest marriage of the ten siblings. The tree had the forenames right and the surname wrong, and the archive's question mark was warranted.
how_it_was_caught: Searching the Devon parish registers instead of trusting the tree. *** The same pass named five brothers-in-law this archive had recorded only as bare surnames - "m. Dalling", "m. Bell", "m. Burton", "m. Sweet", "m. Wood" - and it took under an hour. ***

what_was_said: That the infant William Taylor (29 Dec 1824 - 10 Sep 1825) belonged to GENERATION A, alongside his own father James
what_is_true: *** HE IS GENERATION B - James's son, and the elder brother of the William born in February 1826 who was named after him. *** The error had sat in data/taylor-line.tsv since the file was written.
how_it_was_caught: *** DRAWING THE CHART. *** Nobody had noticed in a fortnight of reading the file as a table, because a table does not care which row is which generation. The moment the same data was rendered as a tree, a dead infant appeared standing beside his father as though he were an uncle. A second way of looking at the same data is a test of it.

what_was_said: Five entries on the places atlas that were not places at all - "SA records", "SA + Argentine records", "GRO + SA records", "Mendoza; later New York and Rio crossings", and one bare dash
what_is_true: *** THEY WERE CITATIONS SITTING IN A PLACE FIELD, and they did TWO kinds of damage at once: *** eight people were missing from the map they belonged on, and four phantom locations were standing on it as though they were towns. Among the eight were PABLO ARMANDO HIMSELF, MARY SEPTIMA, and all three of their sons. *** The central figure of the archive was not on its own atlas. *** Now: Cape Town for the five South Africans, South Africa for Anton, Mendoza for Avelino Carlos, Montevideo for Carolina Oribe. The citations are kept in the notes, not deleted. 37 places became 33.
how_it_was_caught: David read the places data and spotted that the place field held a citation. *** consistency.py now flags any where_found or birthplace that reads like a citation - "records", "GRO", "crossings", "index", or an empty dash - and the check was verified by injecting one. ***

what_was_said: A findmypast harvest plan listing OUTBOUND AND INBOUND PASSENGER LISTS as the second-highest priority, untried
what_is_true: *** THEY WERE TRIED ON 9 SEPTEMBER 2026, under an earlier trial, and the results are in data/passenger-lists.tsv *** - six voyages with masters, ship numbers and TNA references, including the very record this session re-found and briefly believed new: Mary Septima's arrival at Southampton on the RMS Balmoral Castle, 20 May 1935, "C/O Dalling, Fore St, Northam". The eight-year hole had been worked too, with a clean negative and two forenameless candidates.
how_it_was_caught: Checking the archive's own files before writing up the "find". *** The re-find took five minutes; had it not been checked, a source consulted under a previous trial would have been announced as a discovery under this one. *** Read your own sources file before spending a deadline on a source.

what_was_said: That HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR "m. MARY JANE MARSHALL, banns 17 December 1893" - recorded this morning as a marriage, and used to correct a tree's "(? Mary Jane Bridge)"
what_is_true: *** THE BANNS ARE REAL; THE MARRIAGE IS NOT EVIDENCED. *** Banns are an intention to marry. FreeBMD holds NO Horace Taylor marriage in volume 5b - the whole of Devon - between 1893 and 1895. He may have married elsewhere, later, or not to her. *** AND A DECOY NEARLY SETTLED IT THE WRONG WAY: *** a "Taylor, Horace" married a MARSHALL in the same quarter at BOSMERE, SUFFOLK (4a 1487), which would have neatly explained his absence from every Devon census - until the page was read directly and gave the bride as LAURA EMILY MARSHALL, not Mary Jane. Two Taylor-Marshall marriages, one quarter, two counties, two brides.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the volume and page directly instead of trusting the spouse-surname match. *** Before 1912 the GRO index does not print the spouse: FreeBMD infers it from a shared page, so a "match" is an inference and two couples of the same surnames in one quarter will produce a false one. *** FreeBMD is also explicitly incomplete, so the Devon null is softer than the others recorded today.

what_was_said: Every verification run in this session, which took the form "python3 tools/consistency.py | tail -1" and was treated as a gate
what_is_true: *** A PIPELINE EXITS WITH THE STATUS OF ITS LAST COMMAND - "tail" - WHICH ALWAYS SUCCEEDS. *** So consistency.py's exit code gated NOTHING for an entire day. The commits were chained with && behind that pipe, which means a hard contradiction could never have stopped one. It finally showed: an unpaired emphasis marker in errands.tsv was committed while the checker was printing CONTRADICTION on screen - the output was there and had simply scrolled past.
how_it_was_caught: Noticing that a commit succeeded in the same breath as a contradiction was printed. *** Fixed by tools/verify.sh: one script, set -e, no pipes, that runs all five gates and says ALL GATES PASSED or fails. *** The lesson is the archive's own, arriving in a new place: a guard that cannot fail is not a guard - and this time the guard was fine and the way it was CALLED was broken.

what_was_said: Three rows written into errands.tsv with prose in the STATUS column - "*** DONE 14 September 2026 ***", "*** PART READ - 57 of 141 ***", and a whole paragraph - and one row written with three fields where the header has five
what_is_true: *** STATUS IS A CONTROLLED VOCABULARY the errands page looks up: sent, replied, done, ready, waiting-on-david, blocked. *** Anything else falls through to "blocked", so three errands were being published to readers under the wrong chip - including one marked DONE that the page was calling blocked. And the malformed row put its whole detail paragraph into the status column and left detail empty. Now: David / waiting-on-david / the text in its proper field.
how_it_was_caught: *** tools/verify.sh, on its first real run. *** check-links caught the literal markers reaching the errands page, and chasing that exposed the column error behind it. The unpaired-marker check had passed the same row, because a field can be internally consistent and still be the WRONG FIELD.

what_was_said: That DGS 7713386 is 'Indices de bautismos, matrimonios y defunciones, 1726-1800', and that opening it under L was 'THE CHEAPEST TEST IN THE ARCHIVE'
what_is_true: Two images were sampled on 15 September 2026. Image 300 is a burial register of the Catedral Basilica de Montevideo for 1887; image 1500 is a numbered burial register for 1905. Neither is an index and neither is eighteenth century. Two samples out of 2,244 images do not prove the index is absent from the film, but the attribution is not confirmed and the errand must stop calling it cheap or certain.
how_it_was_caught: The attribution came from a catalogue reading, not from the film. The film was never opened until now.

what_was_said: That the castrense chaplain was 'Juan Miguel de Mendoza', and that a neighbouring 1789 entry named an enslaved man belonging to a Llerena
what_is_true: Both were misread at fit-width and corrected at full magnification before either reached the site: the chaplain is JUAN MIGUEL DE BERROETA, and the slave-owner is FRANCISCO JUAREZ, not Llerena. Recorded because the second misreading would have manufactured a Llerena in the regiment's own book - the exact thing this archive wants to find, which is precisely why it nearly got through.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by re-reading at magnification, as the standing rule requires.

what_was_said: That the second column of data/sa-deceased-estates.tsv was a death_year
what_is_true: It is the year the estate was ADVERTISED in the Government Gazette, and the file called it death_year for all eleven rows. Where the J193 has now been read the two differ by years: Ricardo Juan Carlos died 21 December 1994 and was filed under 1996; Anton Armando died 3 April 2003 and was filed under 2013. Column renamed to gazette_year and the true dates recorded.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by reading the actual gazette notices instead of the index that summarised them.

what_was_said: That gendatabase and this archive contradicted each other about Anton Armando Lerena, and might describe two men
what_is_true: There was no contradiction and there is one man. This archive's row read '2013 ... 68', and this session read that as died 2013 aged 68, implying birth about 1945 - but 2013 was the gazette year and 68 was the PAGE NUMBER, both of them columns in the archive's own file. The J193 says: Anton Armando Lerena, born 1952, died 3 April 2003, estate 15127/2013 advertised on page 68 of the gazette of 16 August 2013. gendatabase was right.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by fetching the gazette page that both records were pointing at all along.

what_was_said: That DGS 8166573 held nothing below image 1057
what_is_true: Written this morning from three probes - images 1, 500 and 1000 - all of which happen to fall in the same gap. The film has TWO blocks: images 72-478 and 1057-3295. Block one is the Canelones baptism register 1776-1794, a different item entirely, and this archive already held an ark into it. The claim was not wrong about the images it tested; it was wrong to generalise from three of them.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by resolving an ark the archive already had, which landed at image 274 - inside the range this session had declared empty.

what_was_said: That three images found by the parent-pair query were unread by this archive
what_is_true: All three were already read and recorded, and in fuller words than the index gives - Dominga Josefa's baptism of 1804 with its godparents, Francisco Juan Ramon of 1826, and Lucinda Gregoria of 1827 with the Capitan, the Mayor and a General as godfather. The claim came from inferring an unread ACT from an unread COLLECTION, which does not follow: the same act reaches this archive under different arks by different routes.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by grepping the archive for the names before writing them up as new.

what_was_said: That the 1791 act created 'two Lerena-Aguilar unions in Cordoba' worth reopening the 1754 Granada file for
what_is_true: Only the 1754 groom is Cordoban. His bride, Ana Maria de Aguilar, is of La Mala - La Malaha, in GRANADA province - which this archive had already recorded. Our Rosalia Aguilar is of Cordoba. So the convergence is one very common Andalusian surname in two different provinces, not a family. An earlier session had already run the decisive test - a structured search for a son Sancho de Lerena y Aguilar, returning a controlled No Results Found - and was right to close the file.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by opening the record and finding the archive already held every field on it, including the bride's birthplace.

what_was_said: That Sancho Llerena's last certain appearance as a living man was the deposition of 9 January 1798
what_is_true: Written twice this session, and wrong. The 1812 PADRON is later and is an enumeration of the living: it returns him at calle San Juan No 60, household 59, as Sancho 'andaluz', 45. So the last document that shows him alive is 1812, not 1798, and the unaccounted gap before the trees' death date of 1832 is twenty years rather than thirty-four.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by listing all fourteen records that name him and marking which ones require him to have been standing there.

what_was_said: The blood-relatives chart, as published, drew a family larger than the family is - two Juan Carlos Lerenas, two Maria Lerenas, two Mary Septima Taylors, and Pablo Armando standing beside himself labelled 'aunt or uncle'
what_is_true: Nobody was duplicated in the data. The drawing was. A husband or wife was always drawn as a chip beside the person, with no check that they were already on the chart in their own right - and every married pair of ancestors is two blood relatives, so each got a box AND a chip of the other. *** Nuno Fernando's 13 relatives came out in 22 boxes *** Separately, this register deliberately keeps a row for the mangled machine-index reading of Pablo Armando - 'ARMAND[O] LORENA (as machine-indexed) = Pablo Armando LERENA' - so that the false trail stays visible, and the sibling pass handed that row its own person as a brother. *** A chip is now drawn only for somebody the chart does not already hold, and an alias folds onto the person it is a spelling of *** The same chart is now 14 boxes for 12 people. This was never a Lerena-only fault: counted across every chart in every archive in the estate, *** 218,856 duplicate boxes *** were being drawn, worst in the largest families - Mazza's chart for Frank Mazza drew 232 of its 530 people twice.
how_it_was_caught: David looked at the page and said it made no sense, naming the repeated people. He was right, and it had been published in that state since the page was built. *** No checker could have caught this: every gate in this archive reads data, and the data was correct *** It was the picture that lied.

what_was_said: That a granddaughter of Pablo Armando carries "no Spanish component whatever", and that her Italian is "northern-dominant" - the signature of the Ligurian and Piedmontese emigration to Rosario
what_is_true: Both sentences were written from ONE company's reading. *** On 16 September 2026 the same saliva was read at 23andMe - the account the MyHeritage kit was uploaded from in 2018 - and it disagrees twice. *** It returns *** 2.1% Spanish and Portuguese where MyHeritage returned 0.0% ***, so the flat zero was a fact about a reference panel and not about her DNA. And it puts her Italian in *** SICILY ***, where MyHeritage put it in the north. The northern reading is withdrawn as a DNA argument; the Ligurian names in the Rosario register are still in the Rosario register, but they were never a DNA claim. *** What survives, and is stronger than before: both companies find Italian - 11.1% and 8.0% - in a woman whose other three grandparents are English and Cape Afrikaner. *** One company's zero has been replaced by two companies' agreement, which is a better foundation than the one the hypothesis was built on.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by doing the obvious thing that had never been done: reading the same DNA at the second company that already held it. *** Nothing new was tested and nothing was bought. *** The second reading had been sitting in an account this family already owned since 2018.

what_was_said: Nothing was published from this, because the control caught it first
what_is_true: A battery of twelve surname and place probes was run against the 1,500 DNA relatives at 23andMe - Lerena, Llerena, Lerina, Argentina, Uruguay, Montevideo, Rosario among them - and every single one returned ZERO. *** Before any of them was written down, two controls were run in the same box: BOTHA returned 0, and SOUTH AFRICA returned 0. *** The facets on that same screen show thirty Bothas and 581 relatives with a South African grandparent. The box searches display names and the user's own notes, and nothing else. *** Twelve nulls were one step away from being published as findings, and the control rule stopped all twelve. *** Recorded here as a correction to nothing, because the rule working is worth more on the record than the rule existing.
how_it_was_caught: The control-before-null rule, doing exactly the job it was written for.

what_was_said: A ranked list of archive files to buy at Pretoria, whose top two entries were already in the house
what_is_true: *** This archive drew up a pull list for a researcher going to the National Archives on 22 September, at R2,850 for the first file, and ranked two Transvaal death notices first and second. *** Both had been photographed and saved in David's own folder - Genealogy & Family History/Lerena - *** since November 2021. *** Nobody had ever opened it. Worse than the duplication: the rationale for the second was that it would NAME NUNO FERNANDO'S PARENTS, and *** item 19 of that notice carries the single word "Deceased" and a ditto mark. No names at all. *** The first was ranked to establish Rogue Luis Armando's place of birth; the notice says *** CAPE TOWN ***, and had been saying so for five years. Both are struck from the list, which now leads with two divorce files. *** The same folder also held the 1911 marriage register, which was ON THE WORK LIST as a thing to go and find. ***
how_it_was_caught: Caught because David asked, in as many words, whether this archive had searched the folder. It had not. *** The archive had a register of what it had READ and no register at all of what it already HELD. *** A rule is now on /method/: before any list of documents to acquire, list the documents already held.

what_was_said: That the death notice of Pablo Armando, KAB MOOC 6/9/17017, was the one document that could name Juan Carlos Lerena - and that it had to be fetched from the Western Cape Archives
what_is_true: *** Both halves were wrong, and in opposite directions. *** It did not have to be fetched: a photograph of it had been in David's own files the whole time, while an errand requesting it sat open at the Western Cape Archives. *** And it does not name them. Item 3 reads "Father: not known. Mother: not known." *** The informant was ROSE LILIAN THEYS, who signed as *** "Present at death" and "Executrix Nominate" *** - the woman he lived with at No. 7 Forth Road, described in the liquidation account as a spinster and NO RELATION. She could not name his parents, and none of his three living adult sons supplied them either. *** The archive had built a fortnight of priority around a document whose answer was a null and whose location was a folder. *** One consequence stands: the 1908 Argentine enrolment card is now, definitively, the ONLY document on earth naming Juan Carlos and Maria Lerena.
how_it_was_caught: Found on the same sweep that David prompted, when he asked whether the whole of his Documents folder was worth scouting. It was. *** The archive had never run a filename search for its own subject's name across the disk it was sitting on. ***

what_was_said: That the family had no memory of Pablo Armando's origins beyond "Argentine"
what_is_true: *** They had a surname, and it is not Lerena. *** Sue Rowbotham's Taylor family history, written in England and shared with this family in 2020, records that Mary Septima "went out to South Africa to work for a widower by the name of *** ROBERT (or ROBERTO) MARINO ***". The three sons she names - Louis, Cardo and Nuno - are exactly right, so the memory is anchored in real people; it is the surname that has drifted, or that was never Lerena. *** MARINO is one of the commonest surnames in Italy, and this archive has argued from two companies' DNA readings that he carried Italian ancestry. *** The two lines of evidence are wholly independent and neither knew of the other. *** This is corroboration, not proof, and it is recorded as the former. ***
how_it_was_caught: Read from a Word document in the Taylor folder, on the same sweep. The archive had held it, unopened, for as long as it had held everything else.

what_was_said: That the 1950 records agree with the passport about how old he was
what_is_true: *** They do not, and the disagreement is nine years. *** The Argentine passport and the 1908 enrolment card both give 22 February 1882, which makes him 68 when he died on 19 March 1950. *** The death NOTICE says "77 years - approx". The death CERTIFICATE says "76 years". *** Both South African documents put him in his mid-seventies, and they agree with each other. *** Neither was completed by anyone who knew him: *** the notice by Rose Lilian Theys, no relation, and the certificate by W. Fraser, an undertaker whose stated qualification is "causing burial". The simplest reading is that strangers guessed high, which is what strangers do - and it is recorded rather than smoothed, because in the same folder somebody had filed a Buenos Aires baptism of 1872 for a ROBERTO JUAN ROQUE LLORENS, whose age would fit.
how_it_was_caught: Found on the folder sweep. The archive had transcribed the death notice's other fields this morning and had not stopped at the age.

what_was_said: That the 1872 Buenos Aires baptism of Roberto Juan Roque Llorens was pulled deliberately by the family, as a rival identification they were pursuing
what_is_true: *** Wrong, and it was an inference this archive had no business making. *** The image sat in a folder with no note attached, and this archive wrote that "somebody pulled that deliberately". *** David says it arrived unsolicited, in the mail, from a researcher in Argentina, and that he regards it as likely no relation. *** The document is kept and the working is kept, because the archive had already reached the same verdict from the documents before he said so - and because *** the name has leaked into the MyHeritage family tree, where he is entered as "Roberto Paul (Llorens) Lerena" ***, so the reading is in circulation and is better refuted in public than left to drift.
how_it_was_caught: David said so, plainly, when he read the page. *** The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: a file with no note attached tells you nothing about why it is there, and this archive invented a motive to fill the gap. ***

what_was_said: That the Bailey cluster on the DNA chart is "probably" the BRAYLEY line - Mary Septima Taylor's mother's family
what_is_true: *** Written this morning on a surname resemblance, and tested this afternoon. It does not stand. *** The real Brayley matches were found: "Lisa" of Australia at 23.0 cM sharing BRAYLEY and BAKER, and "Ron Brayley" of the United Kingdom at 16.2 cM sharing BRAYLEY. *** Neither is in cluster 14, and none of the three BAILEY matches in that cluster carries Brayley as an ancestral surname at all. *** The Brayley signal sits at 14-25 cM in Britain and Australia; the Bailey cluster sits at 61-116 cM in the United States. Different signals, different distances, nothing joining them. *** BUT THE ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE EITHER: the Bailey trees hold TWO and FOUR people, and MyHeritage cannot compute a shared surname from a tree with two people in it. *** So the correct statement is that the link is *** UNTESTED, NOT REFUTED *** - and "probably" was more than the evidence carried. The one thing that would settle it is a message to the 116 cM match asking for two generations of names, and that is David's to send.
how_it_was_caught: Caught by running the test instead of admiring the coincidence. *** The GEDCOM handed over the actual Brayley surnames - Brayley, Reed, Wybourn, Temple - and the moment they were put through the match search the Bailey cluster failed to appear among them. ***

what_was_said: Everything this archive published from the GEDCOM it found on the disk - the Brayley ascent, Anton Armando's parentage, Careen Marie's dates, and an Australian birth at Dapto, New South Wales
what_is_true: *** The file was `2018-07 Defranceski.ged`, an eight-year-old backup. David: "Do not use the 2018 gedcom. That is an old backup only. And is incredibly wrong and out of date." *** He was right, and the current export - 15 September 2026, 15,643 individuals against the backup's 8,286 - contradicts it point by point. *** THE AUSTRALIAN BIRTH DOES NOT EXIST: *** the backup put Paul Lerena at DAPTO, WOLLONGONG, NSW on 3 November 1951; the current tree has *** Paul Raymond Lerena, born 11 March 1951 at Johannesburg. *** This archive had flagged that entry as "a date that cannot be true" because his sister was born in Johannesburg six months later - *** the flag was right and the cause was the backup. *** CAREEN MARIE was published as born and died 1945; she was born *** June 1947 and died 22 June 1947 ***, which is what Cheryl told her English cousin in 2020. *** The family were right and the backup was wrong. *** And the backup carried him as "Roberto Paul (Llorens) Lerena, born EST 4 SEP 1872, Argentina" - the unsolicited Buenos Aires candidate baked into his name, his birth date AND his parents. The current tree has restored *** Pablo Armando / Robert Paul Lerena, born 22 February 1882 at Rosario. *** All of it is withdrawn and re-derived from the current export.
how_it_was_caught: David said so plainly. *** The lesson is one this archive should not have needed: a file's DATE IS PART OF ITS PROVENANCE, and "found on the disk" is not a source. *** It was treated as a source because it was large and internally consistent, and it was neither current nor right. The two errors this archive DID catch by internal arithmetic - the impossible Dapto date and a man dead at 117 - should have been read as symptoms rather than as isolated slips.

what_was_said: Nothing yet, and this is a warning rather than a retraction
what_is_true: *** The CURRENT tree still carries Pablo Armando's parents as "Roberto Llorens" and "Francisca Fernandez Lerena" *** - the Buenos Aires couple from the unsolicited Argentine candidate - while his birth has been corrected to *** Rosario, 22 February 1882. *** Those two cannot both be true: the 1872 Buenos Aires baptism is the only thing that ever attached those parents to him, and it is the same document David says is likely no relation. *** The birth was fixed and the parentage was left behind. *** Recorded here so that it is fixed in the tree before it is exported again, and so that no future session mistakes it for evidence. The mother's surname "Fernandez Lerena" appears in no register: the Buenos Aires act says FRANCISCA FERNANDEZ.
how_it_was_caught: Noticed while re-deriving from the current export, by reading the parents field after the birth field instead of stopping at the good news.

what_was_said: *** That the enrolment card's SERIE field reads "3885". *** Published on /enrolment-card/ in the table of what the card says.
what_is_true: *** It reads "E 3555". *** The letter prefix was dropped entirely and two digits were misread. *** The SECCION field, "I 3322", was right *** - and it has the same shape, a letter and four digits, which is what should have prompted the doubt: *** a field transcribed WITHOUT its letter, sitting directly above one transcribed WITH it, is an internal inconsistency this archive should have seen before David did. ***
how_it_was_caught: *** DAVID READ THE ORIGINAL. *** He was asked what the card was telling him, looked at it properly, and sent back both fields. *** Neither number carries any weight in any argument here *** - no conclusion moves - *** but it is logged because a transcription is the one thing this archive asks readers to trust, and a wrong one is worse than a missing one. ***

what_was_said: *** That on /direct-line/, "Above him there is nothing. His parents are unnamed in every document held here." *** Published, and left standing for six days.
what_is_true: *** His parents ARE named. *** The enrolment card gives *** Juan Carlos Lerena and Maria Lerena ***, and has done since 10 September 2026. *** The same page said so in its own opening paragraph *** - "an Argentine army enrolment card... names Pablo Armando's father and mother. For months there was nothing above him. There is now one generation" - *** so the page contradicted itself from top to bottom. *** Now reads "Above him there is ONE GENERATION AND NO MORE", which is the true and still-bleak position: two names, given by their son, and no other record of either anywhere.
how_it_was_caught: *** Caught while rebuilding the front page at David's request. *** Nobody went looking for it. *** This is what a big find does to an archive: the good news gets written at the top of every page and the old despair stays at the bottom, *** and the two sit there disagreeing until someone reads the whole page in one go. *** Graded SERIOUS, not minor: it is not a slipped digit, it is the archive telling a reader the opposite of what it knows, on the page that exists to state the line. ***

what_was_said: *** That work-list row 74 said "the 1908 enrolment card puts him still in Argentina." *** Carried on the work list, unchallenged, while the search for his passage out was framed around it.
what_is_true: *** THE CARD SHOWS THE OPPOSITE. *** Its *Oficina enroladora* reads *** CAPETOWN *** and both *Region Militar* and *Distrito Militar* are *** BLANK *** - the signature of a man registering at his own consulate because he was ALREADY ABROAD. *** The card is evidence he had LEFT Argentina, not that he was in it. *** And the 1908 is unsourced besides: the card bears no year but the class of 1882, sits in a collection catalogued 1911-1936, and the passport gives a Cape Town consular libreta of *** 1915. ***
how_it_was_caught: *** Caught while working row 136. *** The error mattered more than a wrong fact usually does, because *** it set a FLOOR on the search: if he was in Argentina in 1908, his departure is after 1908 *** - and rows 74 and 108 were hunting a 1901-1905 window that the same archive had derived from his son being born at the Cape in 1905. *** The work list was holding two incompatible positions and neither page noticed. *** Graded serious: a wrong fact on a work list is worse than a wrong fact on a page, because a work list tells the next session where to look.

what_was_said: *** That Pablo Armando's absence from the 1895 National Census, at thirteen, suggested he had already left Argentina. *** Written on this archive's own work list earlier the same day.
what_is_true: *** It suggests nothing of the kind, and the archive should have known better within the hour. *** One person can always be missed or mangled by an index - and *** THIS person's name demonstrably mangles. *** The Argentine army's own index turned his enrolment card into *** "ARMAND LORENA", born "Rosario de Lerma, SALTA". *** A boy who can become Armand Lorena on one index can be anything at all on another. *** The absence is consistent with having left and equally consistent with sitting in Rosario under a spelling nobody would think to search. ***
how_it_was_caught: *** Self-caught, about forty minutes after writing it, while running the control on the census. *** *** The control is what separated the two claims: *** a GONZALEZ search returns 88,739 records with the 1895 census reaching Rosario itself, so *** the SURNAME being absent from Santa Fe province is strong *** and *** the INDIVIDUAL being absent is weak. *** Same census, same search, two completely different evidential weights, and it took a control to see it.

what_was_said: *** That FLORES, SAN JOSE, FLORIDA and ROSARIO-COLONIA were "four Uruguayan departments this archive has NEVER SEARCHED", and that the Bernabe Lerena / Casimira Pelaez family of Trinidad was a find. *** Written into data/gedcom-import.tsv, then into work-list row 120, then into data/uruguay-four-departments.tsv, and stated to David in those terms.
what_is_true: *** THE ARCHIVE HAD SEARCHED FLORES THREE DAYS EARLIER AND CALLED IT THE FOUNDING NEST OF THE SURNAME. *** `trinidad-flores-kindred.tsv`, read 13 September 2026, is titled *** "TRINIDAD, DEPARTMENT OF FLORES, URUGUAY - the founding nest of the surname" *** and holds eleven children, the Basque mothers *** BELOQUI, ECHEVERRY and PELAEZ ***, and a correction of its own. `lerena-pelaez-trinidad.tsv` maps four Lerena-Pelaez consanguinity dispensations there. *** BERNABE LERENA AND CASIMIRA PELAEZ ARE IN IT BY NAME. *** San Jose, Florida and Colonia have no dedicated study, so "never searched" was merely too strong for them; for Flores it was simply false.
how_it_was_caught: *** SELF-CAUGHT, about an hour after publishing it, and only because the Flores work led back into `the-three-alejandros.tsv` which cites "the six Trinidad, Flores fathers". *** *** THE MECHANISM IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ERROR: the false claim entered from the GEDCOM import, where a note about what the TREE offered was written as a claim about what the ARCHIVE had done - without checking the archive. *** A statement of the form "this has never been searched" is a claim about 161 data files, and *** it must be grepped before it is written, every time. *** *** WHAT SURVIVES: the record counts, which are new and real - Flores 608, San Jose 315, Florida 231, Colonia 189, against Canelones 191. A nest has been read; a department has not. ***

what_was_said: *** That 23 Geneva Place, Bideford and North Street, Northam were "NOT TESTABLE FREE". *** Written into data/devon-addresses.tsv and worklist row 123 this morning, on the strength of FreeCEN holding neither 1871 nor 1881 for those parishes.
what_is_true: *** THE CENSUS SENTENCE WAS TRUE; THE VERDICT ON TOP OF IT WAS NOT. *** One route was tested and the verdict was written as though all had been. The UK National Archives had never been searched at all, and *** Geneva Place turns out to be a council school whose log books and ADMISSION REGISTERS survive for 1885-1949 *** (North Devon Record Office 629C; also Kew ED 21/26168 and ED 70/427). Admission registers give the child, the date of birth, the father and the address. *** A null must name the routes it tested, and this one silently claimed a route it had not tried. ***
how_it_was_caught: David asked whether this archive had ever looked at nationalarchives.gov.uk. It had not.

what_was_said: *** That 'the other Rosario parishes' were a live route to Pablo Armando's 1882 baptism. *** Offered as one of three remaining routes, and as the second-best of them.
what_is_true: *** THERE WERE NO OTHER PARISHES IN 1882. *** Of the five Rosario parishes, four open in *** 1888, 1896, 1899 and 1899 *** - all after his birth. The Catedral was the only parish in existence, and its register is the one already walked act by act with no Lerena in it. *** The archive's own rosario-five-parishes.tsv said so in a column headed 'does it reach February 1882?', and I recommended the route without reading it. ***
how_it_was_caught: Checked when the route was actually walked, an hour after recommending it.

what_was_said: *** That a birth in February 1882 'should have been registered civilly whether or not he was baptised'. *** Written into worklist row 152 and given to David as the main line on the central question - the one thing left worth doing.
what_is_true: *** CIVIL REGISTRATION IN SANTA FE BEGINS IN 1886. *** Four years after he was born. The act does not exist and no letter will produce it. *** The route is not dead, but the ask had to be rebuilt: a late inscription (inscripción tardía), and above all THE PARENTS' DEATH ACTS ***, which would have been registered because Juan Carlos and María would have died after 1886 - and an Argentine acta de defunción names the parents and spouse of the deceased. *** The corrected route is stronger than the one it replaces. ***
how_it_was_caught: Checked before drafting the letter, because a wrong premise would have wasted the request.

what_was_said: *** That 'only ROSARIO in COLONIA is still unaccounted for', written into worklist row 156 on 20 September when that remainder was split out of row 120. ***
what_is_true: *** ROSARIO-COLLA WAS NEVER UNACCOUNTED FOR. IT IS THE ORIGIN. *** This archive's own notes already read *** 'RAMON LERENA x MARIA JOSEFA GONZALEZ, of ROSARIO / COLLA, fathering children c.1800-1820' *** and *** 'from Rosario-Colla across San Jose, Flores, Florida, Salto'. *** Colonia is not the department the family failed to reach - *** it is the one they came FROM ***, and the 1837 San Jose marriage gives Mauricio's birthplace as COLLA outright. *** The row was written from row 120's summary line without reading the file underneath it ***, which is the same fault as the Rosario-parishes correction three days ago.
how_it_was_caught: Caught while re-measuring Colonia for compound surnames.

what_was_said: *** That the 1812 padron 'records four enslaved people in Sancho's household and GIVES NONE OF THEM A NAME'. *** Carried in this archive's data and on its pages since the padron was first quoted from a published transcription.
what_is_true: *** THE PADRON NAMES ALL FOUR: ANTONIO, JOSE, JUANA and TERESA. *** They are entered after the youngest child *** Dominga *** and before *** RODRIGO FERNANDEZ ***, the father-in-law, who closes the household - and *** Antonio is written out as 'negro esclavo'. *** The claim came from trusting a transcription that dropped them. *** Four people this family held were nameable all along, and this archive said they were not. *** Antonio, Jose and Teresa are now in the register; Juana already was, from the baptism act, and is now corroborated by a second document of the same year.
how_it_was_caught: Read from the image, ark 3:1:3QS7-99ZR-NKNR, 20 September 2026.

what_was_said: *** That the four people standing ABOVE Sancho on the padron - Juana 41, Juan 'negro esclavo', Gabriel and Maria - might be his enslaved household, published on /hypotheses/ for about an hour today. ***
what_is_true: *** WRONG FOUR, AND THE WRONG DIRECTION. *** Those are house *** 59 ***, a different address. Sancho's four are *** below *** his six children. *** The tell was DOMINGA: *** the transcription ends the children at her, so everything between Dominga and Rodrigo Fernandez is the rest of the household. *** The Juana aged 41 in house 59 is a different woman from Sancho's Juana ***, and saying so matters more than the error, because two Juanas on one page is exactly how a family tree acquires a wrong mother.
how_it_was_caught: Caught within the hour by reading downward instead of upward.

what_was_said: *** That film 007499043 has 'EIGHTEEN ITEM BOUNDARIES', published on /uruguay/ and in the film register within the hour. ***
what_is_true: *** IT HAS EIGHTEEN DARK-FRAME CLUSTERS, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME THING. *** The brightness scan separates dark frames (16-30) from ordinary pages (140-156) perfectly - but *** a filming target board is only one kind of dark frame ***, and so are black book covers and spines. *** Image 00127, predicted to be a title board, is a cover; image 00091 is a FIN DEL ITEM card with no title on it. *** *** Only three of the eighteen have been confirmed by eye. *** The scan still did its job - it reduced 3,208 images to eighteen places worth looking - but *** finding candidates was reported as finding boundaries. ***
how_it_was_caught: Caught by testing the inference on the first cluster rather than publishing it untested twice.

what_was_said: *** That the Dominga of the 1836 Montevideo census was 'a candidate, not a finding' and 'attached to Sancho by nothing' - published on /uruguay/, and a NEW PERSON added to the register for her. ***
what_is_true: *** SHE WAS PROVED ON 14 SEPTEMBER AND I DID NOT LOOK. *** The register already held *** DOMINGA JOSEFA LLERENA FERNANDEZ, b. 13 May 1804 ***, daughter of Sancho, wife of *** CAPITAN DON ANTONIO RUIZ DE CARVALLO ***, on the Catedral act of 12 May 1827 - which names her as 'Dona Dominga Llerena de Carvallo' and baptises the very *** LUCINDA *** who appears beside her in the census. *** The duplicate has been removed and its evidence folded into the existing person. *** *** The sting: one hour earlier I declined to add three children of household 97 precisely because they might duplicate people already here - and then created exactly that duplicate by not checking. *** The census and the 1862 Rio de Janeiro marriage remain genuine additions.
how_it_was_caught: Caught while chasing which parish register rows 167 and 168 were blocked on.

what_was_said: *** That the Gilberto Lerena who landed at Buenos Aires on 27 February 1928 was 'Not in the 1895 census household of Gilberto (1854)' *** - stated as fact in the register, and the only thing holding his row apart from another row in the same register.
what_is_true: *** HE MAY WELL BE IN IT. *** Line 6 of that schedule reads *** "Salvanach Lerena, GILBERTO", varon, 17, soltero, R. Oriental *** - the eldest son, born 1877 or 1878 against the arrival's 1879, already in this register as Gilberto LERENA Salvanach (the younger). The schedule had been read as a household on 14 September and the objection was never checked against it. *** The two rows are now cross-referenced and the test named; they are NOT merged, because both are index-level. ***
how_it_was_caught: The duplicate gate flagged the pair, and working the backlog meant reading the household file that the objection rested on
retired: Not in the 1895 census household of Gilberto (1854)

what_was_said: *** That the baptism of ALEJANDRO at La Mauricia dates him to 29 May 1843, and that this 'pushes their marriage back before May 1843' *** - the marriage of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel, stated in the register since 14 September.
what_is_true: *** THE YEAR ON THAT PAGE IS A FORMULA. *** Read end to end at magnification on 20 September, all three acts of 7 January 1846 give the birth year in the identical words, *** "del pasado ano cuarenta y tres" *** - and the third is for a different couple. The phrase contradicts itself, since the acts open "En siete de Enero de mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis" and "el pasado ano" is then 1845. And it cannot be literally true: the two children of Luis and Justiniana on the page would be born *** five months and ten days apart ***. Nothing outside the page dates Alejandro, so his birth is *** undetermined between 1843 and 1845 *** and the safe floor for the marriage is *** before May 1845 ***.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the page for a different reason - chasing why a father and son both carried 9 February as a birth day - and magnifying the numerals instead of trusting two transcripts already in the archive
retired: pushes their marriage back before May 1843

what_was_said: *** That the 1843 reading was retracted on 14 September and the archive moved on. *** Five data files went on asserting "9 February 1843" for six days, one of them arguing for it in a paragraph headed WHAT THIS SETTLES, and the correction's `retired` column was left empty so no gate enforced it.
what_is_true: *** A CORRECTION THAT IS NOT CARRIED BACK TO THE FILE THE READING CAME FROM IS NOT A CORRECTION. *** All five now say 1845 or quote the old reading; correction 50 has its `retired` column filled, and check-corrections.py enforces it. Also withdrawn: "Eleven months before Luis Eugenio was born on 9 February 1843. The fit is exact." - the marriage of 3 March 1842 is followed by *** Justiniana Mauricia, sixteen months later ***, and Luis Eugenio is the second child at thirty-five months.
how_it_was_caught: Grepping data/ for the retracted string while chasing an unrelated date

what_was_said: *** That work-list row 111 read "TAB MHG 1095/48 - tell Anne before Tuesday, its death notice is already in the house", with every limit on it kept in the note. *** And that the note then said "the other four on her list" while listing five.
what_is_true: *** THE ROW WAS ACTIONED AS "STOP", AND THE WHOLE BOOYZEN PULL AT PRETORIA WAS CALLED OFF. *** The finding was that ONE document of the six-estate list is already in the house - the death notice of 1095/48. Cancelled with it were the *** will and liquidation account of that same estate ***, which nobody holds, and *** five entire estates *** - 3734/46, 769/52, 5155/51, 10/57 and 52653 - none of which is in the folder. *** A row whose headline reads as an instruction and whose limits live in a note is a badly written row, *** and this archive wrote it. The headline now states the scope, the miscount is fixed, and the row says what it cost.
how_it_was_caught: David asked why Anne had been told to stop, which did not match what this row actually found

what_was_said: *** That ALFREDO JUSTINIANO LERENA TRAIBEL was born in March 1858, and that "his baptismal age of 1858 sits oddly against the 35 he gave at his 1892 marriage". *** The register blamed the discrepancy on the record and on "ages at marriage", the weakest date in genealogy.
what_is_true: *** BORN 2 OCTOBER 1856, ON THE ACT THIS ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY READ. *** Re-read off the image on 20 September - film 007713686 image 2847 - it says *** "que nacio el dia DOS de OCTUBRE ... cincuenta y seis" ***. The baptism date had been written into the birth column. *** AND THE AGE WAS NEVER ODD: *** a man born 2 October 1856 is exactly THIRTY-FIVE on 3 February 1892, which is what he told the priest. The record agreed with itself the whole time.
how_it_was_caught: A FamilySearch search run for an unrelated reason printed "Birth 2 October 1856" beside the christening of 12 March 1858

what_was_said: *** That ANA ROSARIO LERENA TRAIBEL was born in March 1858 and was 'probably twins' with her brother Alfredo Justiniano ***, both baptised at San Francisco de Asis on 12 March 1858.
what_is_true: *** BORN 14 JANUARY 1855 - and they are twenty-one months apart. *** Her own act, on the same opening, reads *** "que nacio el dia CATORCE de ENERO ... cincuenta y cinco" ***. She was carried to the font at THREE YEARS OLD and her brother at seventeen months. *** "Probably twins" was an inference from a shared baptism date and the acts refute it *** - this family baptised in batches, years late, and did it at La Mauricia in 1846 as well. The same inference is attached to the two MORATORIO girls of 1880 and is now flagged there as untested.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the second act on an image already open for the first

what_was_said: *** That this register held THREE separate people for Carlos Augusto Federico Lerena Salvanach, TWO for Avelino Carlos Lerena and TWO for Rosa Maria Eppens *** - and that data/relations.tsv gave Carlos a wife and a son the register had already ruled out.
what_is_true: *** SEVEN ROWS WERE FOUR PEOPLE. *** The archive had done every identification and none of the merges: one note read *** "two independent sources, same couple" ***, another *** "see the CEMLA row for the same man" ***, a third *** "the 'Rosa M. E. Lerena' of the CEMLA list" ***. The arithmetic confirms the hardest of them - the Retiro act of 25 March 1914 calls him *** "de treinta anos" ***, and a man born 9 July 1883 is exactly thirty that March. *** AND THE EDGES WERE WORSE THAN THE ROWS: *** relations.tsv made him the husband of ADELA CAMIGLIA and father of AVELINO CARLOS at Mendoza, which the Rosa Maria Eppens row had explicitly denied since 14 September - *** "two men, one name, and the register now says so on both rows." *** It said so on the rows and nothing told the edges. The Mendoza man now has a row of his own, and they point at him.
how_it_was_caught: Working the duplicate backlog pair by pair, which is what that backlog is for

what_was_said: *** That lines 10-13 of Gilberto Lerena's 1895 census schedule give the ages '6, 6, 5, 2' *** - published in data/1895-census-gilberto-household.tsv and used to keep three register rows apart.
what_is_true: *** THEY ARE 8, 6, 5, 2. MARIA A. IS EIGHT. *** Read off the image at magnification on 20 September, film 004149111 image 8. *** AND THAT ONE DIGIT SETTLED TWO IDENTIFICATIONS. *** At six, Maria A. could not be MARIA ANGELICA JULIA LERENA SALVANACH, baptised 31 October 1886; at eight she is exactly that. MARIA C., six, is MARIA CARLOTA, baptised at about a year old on 29 October 1890 - and her nacion column reads ARGENTINA, which is what that baptism row has always claimed for her. Both are merged, with LUIS F. and CARLOS A. earlier the same day. *** The enumerator wrote initials and the priest wrote names, and this archive held four of these children twice. ***
how_it_was_caught: Working the duplicate backlog: two pairs were blocked on a single digit, so the image was opened

what_was_said: *** That 'Juan Carlos Lerena as a named person, any role, any country, any collection' returns ONE record and it is not him, and that there is 'no indexed child of ANY man recorded exactly as Juan Carlos Lerena'. *** Published on /direct-line/ since 17 September, in the table that carries this archive's central null.
what_is_true: *** BOTH RETURN TWO NOW, AND THE SECOND IS HIM. *** Re-run 21 September while testing the exact-forename trap: *** "Juan Carlos Lerena, Father, Argentina Military Records 1911-1936, spouse MARIA LERENA, child PABLO ARMANDO LERENA" *** - ark 1:1:6TH8-DVXH, which is the 1908 enrolment card and a record THIS ARCHIVE HAS CITED SINCE IT FOUND IT. *** NOTHING WAS WRONG WITH THE SEARCHES. *** The Argentina Military Records index has since gained the card; its FamilySearch citation reads 16 September 2026, the day after the test. *** WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: *** Juan Carlos still has no record of his own - no birth, no marriage, no death - and the new hit is his son's record naming him as a father. *** WHAT DOES: *** he is findable by name now, and the index places him at "Rosario de Lerma, SALTA", the error this archive corrected on 13 September.
how_it_was_caught: Re-running the central null in the fuzzy-forename/exact-surname shape, which is work list row 157 - the trap sweep found the archive's own document instead

what_was_said: *** That ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA LARRIERA, born in the Departamento de San Jose on 4 November 1880, 'is NOT ours' - published in her register row since 14 September 2026, which added that her father Alberto Lerena 'would be the right age to be ALBERTO OCTAVIO LERENA LENGUAS' and that 'NOTHING JOINS THEM but a forename and an age'. ***
what_is_true: *** SHE IS OURS, and the candidate was the wrong man. *** Alberto Lerena's own Montevideo death registration of 2 March 1921, certificate 246, names his wife MARIA INES LARRIERA and his parents AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA TREIBEL. So Zelmira's father is PEDRO ALBERTO YSABELINO LERENA TRAIBEL, baptised at the Aguada on 21 November 1852, and she is a GREAT-GRANDDAUGHTER OF SANCHO - through Avelino, not through Luis. *** The row was right that the question turned on her father and right to refuse the guess; it was wrong to write off the person while the question was open. *** Seven brothers and sisters of hers were entered the same day. *** THE LINK WAS INDEX-LEVEL FOR ABOUT AN HOUR. *** The 1921 image was opened the same day - film 008165205 image 01604 - and reads 'Que el finado era hijo de AVELINO LERENA, fallecido, y de AMBROSIA TREIBEL, fallecida', and then counts NUEVE HIJOS and names them. So the retraction above stands on an image, and the act supplied a NINTH child the index never showed. See data/alberto-lerena-larriera.tsv.

what_was_said: *** That Alfredo Justiniano Lerena Traibel married *** "HERMENEGILDA CAROLINA GAVARRO" ***, daughter of *** "Don GERONIMO GAVARRO" *** and *** "Dona CAROLINA JUAREZ" *** - three register rows, a dispensation table, the 1892 working log and the last-attested-alive file, published since 14 September 2026. ***
what_is_true: *** ALL THREE SURNAMES ARE WRONG, AND THE FAULT IS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN RULE, UNKEPT. *** The 1892 marriage act was recorded as FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ - a MACHINE transcript - and the image was never opened, which is the one thing this archive says it always does. The image was opened on 21 September 2026: film 007713383, image 02601, folio 340. It reads *** 'hija legitima de Don GERONIMO GAVAZZO y Dona CAROLINA SUAREZ' ***. *** So she is a GAVAZZO and her mother a SUAREZ. *** It is corroborated by a second image forty-eight years later - her own Montevideo death registration of 20 June 1940, which writes her HERMENEGILDA GAVAZZO DE LERENA with the same two parents. Two images against one machine transcript. *** GAVAZZO is a known Montevideo surname and GAVARRO is not, which is exactly the kind of tell that should have prompted the check earlier. ***

what_was_said: *** That MARIA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS, Sancho's wife, was born at *** "Montevideo" *** - the birthplace this register carried for her, and the place the atlas put her. ***
what_is_true: *** SHE WAS NATURAL DE ASTURIAS, and this archive had known it for a week without changing the row. *** The 1811 baptism of her son Luis Escolastico reads 'y de D.a MARIA [Fernandez] nat.l de ASTURIAS'. data/1811-luis-baptism-act.tsv recorded that on 14 September 2026; the register was never updated, so the correction existed and never propagated - the exact fault this archive has a standing rule about. *** IT ALSO CHANGES THE FAMILY'S SHAPE: both halves of Sancho's household were SPANISH IMMIGRANTS, from opposite ends of Spain *** - Andalusia and Asturias - meeting at Montevideo. And her parents RODRIGO FERNANDEZ and ROSA FERNANDEZ, named on the same act, had never been entered as people either. Read off the plate 21 September 2026: film 007713375 image 02410.
